record.title: Multiplicity conjecture for Schubert varieties at arbitrary points
record.statement:
Let $w,\tau\in W/W_{P_d}$. Let $R^+$ and $R_{P_d}^+$ denote the positive roots of the ambient root system and of the parabolic subsystem, respectively. Define $S'_{w,\tau}$ to be the unisets of $(R^+\setminus R_{P_d}^+)^{\ast}$ satisfying the condition that, for every chain of commuting reflections $s_{\alpha_1}>\cdots>s_{\alpha_t}$ with $s_{\alpha_i}\in S'_{w,\tau}$, one has $w\geq\tau s_{\alpha_1}\cdots s_{\alpha_t}$. Let $M$ be the maximum cardinality of an element of $S'_{w,\tau}$. **Multiplicity conjecture.** The multiplicity of $X(w)$ at $\tau$ is

$$
\operatorname{mult}_{\tau}X(w)=|\\{S\in S'_{w,\tau}:|S|=M\\}|.
$$

This conjecture gives a combinatorial formula for the multiplicity of a Schubert variety at an arbitrary point, using maximal unisets satisfying the Bruhat-order condition. Its status is unresolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: V. Kreiman and V. Lakshmibai, “Multiplicities of Singular Points in Schubert Varieties of Grassmannians”, arXiv:math/0108071 (2001).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0108071

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2001).

record.title: The M-regularity index conjecture for syzygies of abelian varieties
record.statement:
Let $X$ be an abelian variety and let $A$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. The **M-regularity index** $m(A)$ is the largest integer $l$ such that

$$
A\otimes \mathfrak m_{x_1}^{k_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathfrak m_{x_p}^{k_p}
$$

is $M$-regular for all distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_p\in X$ with $\sum k_i=l$. Here a line bundle satisfies property $N_p$ when its embedding has the corresponding syzygy property. **The M-regularity index conjecture.** If $p\ge m$ are non-negative integers and $m(A)\ge m$, then

$$
A^{\otimes k}\text{ satisfies }N_p\quad\text{for every }k\ge p+3-m.
$$

This proposes a general relationship between the higher-order properties of an ample line bundle and the equations and syzygies of the associated embedding. The source presents it as a natural question raised by the preceding syzygy theorem; its resolution is not specified here.
record.source_name: Giuseppe Pareschi and Mihnea Popa, “Regularity on abelian varieties II: basic results on linear series and defining equations”, arXiv:math/0110004 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0110004

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2001).

record.title: Existence conjecture for independent-set densities in sparse random graphs
record.statement:
Let ${\bf {\cal I}}(n,c)$ denote the maximum size of an independent set in the Erdős–Rényi random graph $G(n,c/n)$, and let ${\bf {\cal I}}(n,r)$ denote the maximum size of an independent set in a random $r$-regular graph. The parameters satisfy $c>0$ and $r\geq 3$.

**Independent-set density existence conjecture.** For every $c>0$ and $r\geq 3$, the limits

$$
\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}{\mathbb{E}[{\bf {\cal I}}(n,c)]\over n}, \qquad \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}{\mathbb{E}[{\bf {\cal I}}(n,r)]\over n}
$$

exist.

The conjecture concerns the existence of limiting expected independent-set densities in both sparse Erdős–Rényi and random regular graphs. The supplied text says that it remains a conjecture and attributes it to prior work by Aldous and Steele and to Aldous's collection of open problems.
record.source_name: David Gamarnik, Tomasz Nowicki and Grzegorz Swirscsz, “Maximum Weight Independent Sets and Matchings in Sparse Random Graphs. Exact Results using the Local Weak Convergence Method”, arXiv:math/0309441 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309441

record.title: Conjecture on the middle-degree Bockstein and injectivity of the second Bockstein
record.statement:
Let $N$ be an integer, let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be the differentials in the spectral sequence under consideration, and let $HH_i^\sigma(\mathcal{A})$ denote the twisted Hochschild homology groups. For $0\leq i\leq N$, write $\omega_1(N,i)$ and $\omega_2(N,i)$ for the indicated generators, and let $f:\operatorname{ker}(B_0)\to HH_3^\sigma(\mathcal{A})$ be the map appearing in the spectral sequence.

**Bockstein conjecture.** For $N$ even,

$$
[B_1(\omega_1(N,\tfrac{1}{2}N))]\neq 0\in HH_2^\sigma(\mathcal{A}),
$$

and this class is proportional to $[\omega_2(N,\tfrac{1}{2}N)]$. For all $N$, the map

$$
B_2:HH_2^\sigma(\mathcal{A})/\operatorname{im}(B_1)\longrightarrow HH_3^\sigma(\mathcal{A})
$$

is injective. Consequently, for $N$ odd, the map

$$
f:\operatorname{ker}(B_0)\longrightarrow HH_3^\sigma(\mathcal{A})
$$

is zero.

These expected properties would determine the relevant differentials in the spectral sequence and hence clarify the computation of the twisted cyclic homology groups. The source explicitly states that no proof is currently available; the status of both assertions is therefore open.
record.source_name: Tom Hadfield and Ulrich Kraehmer, “Twisted homology of quantum SL(2)”, arXiv:math/0405249 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0405249

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2004).

record.title: Rationality conjecture for Jacobian points and twisted Eisenstein series
record.statement:
Let $X_0(l)$ be the modular curve with its natural ${\mathbb Q}$-structure and Jacobian, and let $h$ determine the degree-zero twist sheaf ${\mathcal F}_0(h)$ on $X_0(l)$. For each weight $k$, write $E_{k,i;h}$ for the associated twisted Eisenstein series, indexed by $i$, and let $R_k(q)$ be a formal power series.

**Rationality conjecture.** The sheaf ${\mathcal F}_0(h)$ gives a rational point on the Jacobian if and only if, for each $k$, there exists a nonzero formal power series $R_k(q)$ such that all coefficients of $E_{k,i;h}R_k(q)$ are rational for every $i$. Equivalently, the ratios

$$
\frac{E_{k,i;h}}{E_{k,j;h}}
$$

have rational Fourier coefficients for all $k$, $i$, and $j$ whenever $E_{k,j;h}\not\equiv 0$.

This conjecture proposes that rationality of the Jacobian point represented by the twisted sheaf is exactly detected by rational Fourier-coefficient data from the associated twisted Eisenstein series. The abstract gives the equivalent formulation in terms of ratios of twisted Eisenstein series, while the supplied text provides no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Lev A. Borisov, “Holomorphic Eisenstein series with Jacobian twists”, arXiv:math/0410333 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410333

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2004).

record.title: The abelian Lehmer problem
record.statement:
Let $A/K$ be an abelian variety over a number field and let $
\mathcal{L}$ be a symmetric ample line bundle on $A$. For $P\in A(\overline{K})$, let $\delta_{\mathcal{L},K}(P)$ denote the obstruction index relative to $\mathcal{L}$ and $K$, and let $g_0$ be the dimension of the smallest algebraic subgroup containing $P$.

**Abelian Lehmer problem.** There is a constant $c(A/K,\mathcal{L})>0$ such that, for every point $P\in A(\overline{K})$ of infinite order modulo every proper abelian subvariety of $A$,

$$
\widehat{h}_{\mathcal{L}}(P)\geq\frac{c(A/K,\mathcal{L})}{\delta_{\mathcal{L},K}(P)}.
$$

Moreover, for every nontorsion point $P\in A(\overline{K})$, with $D=[K(P):K]$,

$$
\widehat{h}_{\mathcal{L}}(P)\geq\frac{c(A/K,\mathcal{L})}{D^{1/g_0}}.
$$

This is a Lehmer-type lower bound for canonical heights on abelian varieties with complex multiplication. The source presents it as a problem and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Nicolas Ratazzi, “Intersection de courbes et de sous-groupes, et problèmes de minoration de hauteur dans les variétés abéliennes C.M”, arXiv:math/0502186 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0502186

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2005).

record.title: The eight-point maximum conjecture for the three-dimensional angular sum
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Q}_N$ denote the configuration space of $N$ points in $d$-dimensional space, and let $F_N$ be the angular sum defined in the paper. **The eight-point maximum conjecture.** For $d=3$,

$$
\sup_{\mathcal{Q}_8}F_8=16\left[\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}+\frac{4(1+\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5+4\sqrt{2}}}+\frac{3+2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5+4\sqrt{2}}}-\frac{1}{5+4\sqrt{2}}\right]\simeq79.501.
$$

The maximum is attained when the eight points form two identical unit-edge squares in parallel planes separated by $h=\sqrt{1+2\sqrt{2}}/2$, with the axis joining their centers perpendicular to the squares and the squares rotated relative to one another by $\pi/4$. This is a numerical conjecture about the maximizing configuration; the paper compares it with the cube, whose value is slightly smaller.
record.source_name: Amaury Mouchet, “Upper and lower bounds for an eigenvalue associated with a positive eigenvector”, arXiv:math/0505541 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505541

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2005).

record.title: The shifting conjecture for non-reverse-lexicographic term orders
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a polynomial ring, let $\succ$ be a term order on $S$ other than the graded reverse lexicographic order, and let $k\geq 2$ be the smallest degree on which $\succ$ and the reverse lexicographic order disagree. For each finite index $i$, let $m_i$ be the $i$th squarefree monomial of degree $k$ with respect to the reverse lexicographic order, and set

$$
I_i:=\langle m_1,\ldots,m_i\rangle.
$$

Let $i_0\geq 1$ be the smallest index for which $I_{i_0}$ is not a US$\succ$I. **The shifting conjecture.** Then

$$
\Delta_{\succ}(I_{i_0})\neq I_{i_0}.
$$

This conjecture would give a negative answer to whether a term order other than reverse lexicographic order can satisfy $\Delta_{\succ}(I)=I$ for every squarefree strongly stable ideal. The preceding results establish the corresponding affirmative statement for US$\succ$I ideals and show that USLIs are fixed by every term order, while the proposed assertion remains unproved in the source.
record.source_name: Eric Babson, Isabella Novik and Rekha R. Thomas, “Reverse Lexicographic and Lexicographic Shifting”, arXiv:math/0507565 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0507565

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2005).

record.title: Villarreal's torsion-free quotient conjecture for uniform clutters
record.statement:
Let $A$ be a $\{0,1\}$-matrix whose columns each contain the same number $d\geq 2$ of $1$'s, with column vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_q$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the clutter associated with $A$, and let $\mathcal{C}'$ range over all minors of $\mathcal{C}$. For each minor, let $\alpha_0(\mathcal{C}')$ be the smallest cardinality of a minimal vertex cover and let $\beta_1(\mathcal{C}')$ be the maximum number of pairwise independent edges. **Villarreal's conjecture.** If

$$
\alpha_0(\mathcal{C}')=\beta_1(\mathcal{C}')
$$

for every minor $\mathcal{C}'$ of $\mathcal{C}$, then

$$
\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}/\big((v_1,1),\ldots,(v_q,1)\big)
$$

is torsion-free.
The source describes this as a weaker conjecture following a proposition that reducedness of the associated graded ring forces the displayed quotient group to be torsion-free. Its resolution status is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: I. Gitler, C. E. Valencia and R. H. Villarreal, “A note on Rees algebras and the MFMC property”, arXiv:math/0511307 (2007).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0511307

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2005).

record.title: The combinatorial characterization conjecture for the matroid invariant
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a loop- and co-loop-free matroid, let $\operatorname{Poly}_M$ be its matroid polytope, and let $G_M$ be a polynomial assigned to each isomorphism class of such matroids. For a polyhedral decomposition $\mathcal{D}$ of $\operatorname{Poly}_M$ into smaller matroid polytopes, let $\mathring{\mathcal{D}}$ denote the set of interior faces. A series-parallel matroid is understood in the standard sense.

**Combinatorial characterization conjecture.** If the assignment $M\mapsto G_M$ satisfies
1. for every such decomposition,

$$
G_M=\sum_{\operatorname{Poly}_F\in\mathring{\mathcal{D}}}G_F,
$$

2. if $M$ is a direct sum of $c$ series-parallel matroids, then

$$
G_M=t^c,
$$

then $G_M=g_M$.

This conjecture asks whether the stated valuation and normalization properties uniquely determine the invariant $g_M$. The source calls it essentially combinatorial and supplies no resolution evidence, so it remains open.
record.source_name: David E Speyer, “A matroid invariant via the K-theory of the Grassmannian”, arXiv:math/0603551 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603551

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2006).

record.title: Minimal layered-triangulation conjecture for the solid torus
record.statement: Let $p/q$ be a reduced rational number with $0\leq p\leq q$, including the exceptional forms $0/1$ and $1/1$. A **$p/q$-layered-triangulation** is a layered-triangulation of the solid torus extending the one-vertex $p/q$-triangulation on its boundary, and a minimal triangulation means one using the fewest tetrahedra among all triangulations with the specified boundary extension. **Minimal layered-triangulation conjecture for the solid torus.** The minimal triangulation of the solid torus that extends the $p/q$-triangulation on the boundary is the minimal $p/q$-layered-triangulation of the solid torus. The authors describe this as a compelling conjecture they have been unable to confirm, so the question is whether layered-triangulations realize the minimum possible number of tetrahedra for every prescribed boundary triangulation.
record.source_name: William Jaco and J. Hyam Rubinstein, “Layered-triangulations of 3-manifolds”, arXiv:math/0603601 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603601

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2006). “This conjecture is one of the compelling open problems.”

record.title: The two-dimensional kings graph half-dependent density conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\rho(G)=h(G)/|V(G)|$ be the maximum density among half-dependent sets in $G$. For the two-dimensional kings graph $K^{(2)}[n]$, write

$$
\rho^{(2)}(n)=\rho(K^{(2)}[n]),\qquad \rho^{(2)}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\rho^{(2)}(n).
$$

**Two-dimensional kings graph density conjecture.** The half-dependent limiting density is

$$
\rho^{(2)}=\frac{3}{5},
$$

and, for all $n$ and some constant $C$ independent of $n$,

$$
\rho^{(2)}(n)\geq \frac{3}{5}-\frac{C}{n^2}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the maximum density of half-dependent sets, equivalently configurations of kings, on standard non-toroidal two-dimensional boards. The paper states it as the motivating conjecture and seeks exact limiting densities and finite-board bounds; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Eugen J. Ionascu, Dan Pritikin and Stephen E. Wright, “k-Dependence and Domination in Kings Graphs”, arXiv:math/0608140 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608140

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

record.title: Faber-Pandharipande conjecture on the prime valuations of intersection-number denominators
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal D_g$ be the least common multiple of the denominators of the genus-$g$ intersection numbers, and let $\operatorname{ord}(p,n)$ denote the maximum integer such that $p^{\operatorname{ord}(p,n)}\mid n$. For a prime number $p$ and $g\geq 2$, the conjecture asserts:

**Faber–Pandharipande conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ord}(2,\mathcal D_g)=3g+\operatorname{ord}(2,g!),
$$

$$
\operatorname{ord}(3,\mathcal D_g)=g+\operatorname{ord}(3,g!),
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{ord}(p,\mathcal D_g)=\left\lfloor\frac{2g}{p-1}\right\rfloor\quad\text{for }p\geq 5,
$$

where $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer not exceeding $x$. These formulas give the conjectural exact values of the common denominators of tautological intersection numbers on the moduli space of stable curves; the source reports computations only through genus $20$, so the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Kefeng Liu and Hao Xu, “Intersection numbers and automorphisms of stable curves”, arXiv:math/0608209 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0608209

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2006).

record.title: Schilling–Shimozono conjecture for the branching-component automorphism
record.statement: Let $D$ be a $\pm$ diagram of shape $\Lambda/\lambda$ whose ambient $r\times s$ rectangle has complement of $\Lambda$ tiled by vertical dominos. Let $m_{i}^{\circ}$, $m_{i}^{+}$, $m_{i}^{-}$ and $m_{i}^{\pm}$ count columns of height $i$ having respectively no symbol, a $+$, a $-$, or a $\pm$ pair. If $r$ is even, define $m_{0}^{\circ}=s-\Lambda_{1}$. For $i\equiv r+1\pmod 2$, all $m_i^*$ with $*\in\{\circ,+,-,\pm\}$ vanish. **Schilling–Shimozono conjecture.** The automorphism $\check{\sigma}(D)$ is the $\pm$ diagram with, for every $0\leq i\leq r$, $m_{i+2}^{\pm}$ empty columns of height $i$, $m_i^-$ columns of height $i$ carrying a $+$, $m_i^+$ columns of height $i$ carrying a $-$, and $m_i^\circ$ columns of height $i+2$ carrying a $\pm$ pair. This gives the conjectural shape-preserving automorphism of the branching component graph used to construct the affine crystal automorphism.
record.source_name: Philip Sternberg, “Applications of Crystal Bases to Current Problems in Representation Theory”, arXiv:math/0610704 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610704

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2006).

record.title: The adjacent vertex distinguishing chromatic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple connected graph, and let $d45e$ denote its maximum degree. An **adjacent vertex distinguishing coloring** (or avd-coloring) is a proper edge coloring such that, for every pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, the sets of colors on edges incident with $u$ and $v$ are different. The avd-chromatic number is the minimum number of colors in an avd-coloring of $G$.

**Zhang's conjecture.** If $G\neq C_5$ and $G\neq K_2$, where $C_5$ is the cycle of size $5$, then the avd-chromatic number of $G$ is at most

$$
\Delta+2.
$$

Here $\Delta$ is the maximum degree of $G$. The conjecture concerns the number of colors required when incident edges must be properly colored while adjacent vertices receive distinct incident color sets; the supplied source gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Hamed Hatami, “Δ+300 is a Bound on the Adjacent Vertex Distinguishing Edge Chromatic Number”, arXiv:math/0701012 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701012

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).

record.title: The MSV sheaf conjecture for Gorenstein toroidal varieties
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a variety with only Gorenstein toroidal singularities. Let $\mathcal{MSV}(X)$ denote the proposed sheaf of string-differential forms, locally modeled on the product of the corresponding sheaves for an open ball and for a singularity. Its $L[0]=0$ component carries a grading and a differential generalizing the de Rham differential, and its hypercohomology is the associated string cohomology.

**MSV sheaf conjecture.** For every variety $X$ with only Gorenstein toroidal singularities, there exists a local sheaf $\mathcal{MSV}(X)$ locally isomorphic to the product of $\mathcal{MSV}(\operatorname{open\ ball})$ and $\mathcal{MSV}(\operatorname{singularity})$. The construction depends on the parameters $g_n$ and perhaps on other structures yet to be determined. The sheaf has the structure of a sheaf of conformal vertex algebras, with an $N=2$ structure if $X$ is Calabi--Yau. The hypercohomology of its $L[0]=0$ complex has dimensions prescribed by the cited results and possesses a pure Hodge structure if $X$ is projective.

The conjecture aims to construct a generalized chiral de Rham-type sheaf on varieties with Gorenstein toroidal singularities and recover the expected string-theoretic and Hodge-theoretic invariants. The source calls the definition provisional and says that more work is necessary.
record.source_name: Lev A. Borisov, “Vertex Algebras and Mirror Symmetry”, arXiv:math/9809094 (1999).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9809094

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 1998).

record.title: The character bound conjecture for high-dimensional irreducible representations of symmetric groups
record.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group. An irreducible representation (irrep) $\lambda$ of $S_n$ has dimension $d_\lambda$ and character $\chi_\lambda$. For a permutation $\pi\in S_n$, let $s(\pi)$ be its support, let $c(\pi)$ be the number of its nontrivial cycles, and let $t(\pi)=s(\pi)-c(\pi)$ be the minimum number of transpositions whose product is $\pi$. Call $\lambda$ **big** if

$$
d_\lambda>e^{-\sqrt{n}\log n}\sqrt{n!}.
$$

**Character bound conjecture.** There is a constant $A$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, every big $\lambda$ satisfies

$$
\left|\frac{\chi_\lambda(\pi)}{d_\lambda}\right|\le A^{t(\pi)}n^{-t(\pi)/2}
$$

for all $\pi\in S_n$.

This conjectured uniform estimate for normalized characters of sufficiently high-dimensional irreducible representations would imply the required smoothness bounds for typical representations and support the analysis of quantum sieve algorithms for Graph Isomorphism. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Cristopher Moore and Alexander Russell, “On the Impossibility of a Quantum Sieve Algorithm for Graph Isomorphism”, arXiv:quant-ph/0609138 (2006).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0609138

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2006).

record.title: Conjecture on the non-integer BP solution for the permanent
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonnegative matrix, let $T_c$ be the critical temperature from Proposition 1, and let $\beta_i^j$ denote a solution of the belief-propagation (BP) equations on the edge set $E$. The solution under consideration is the non-integer BP solution that emerges from the maximum-likelihood configuration at $T=T_c$.

**Non-integer BP solution conjecture.** The non-integer solution extends beyond the small $T_c+\varepsilon$ vicinity of $T_c$ and transitions smoothly as $T\to\infty$ into the fully homogeneous solution

$$
\beta_i^j=1/N\quad\text{for all }(i,j)\in E.
$$

Moreover, no other non-integer solutions exist for $T<T_c$; consequently, when this solution emerges at $T=T_c$, it gives a global minimum of the belief-propagation free energy.

This conjecture concerns the global continuation and uniqueness of the non-integer BP solution beyond the local analysis near the critical temperature. The source presents these claims as plausible conjectures and does not provide a resolution.
record.source_name: Yusuke Watanabe and Michael Chertkov, “Belief Propagation and Loop Calculus for the Permanent of a Non-Negative Matrix”, arXiv:0911.1419 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.1419

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2009).

record.title: Humphreys' support variety conjecture for tilting modules
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the reductive algebraic group, $G_1$ its first Frobenius kernel, $h$ the Coxeter number, and $W_p^+$ the set of minimum-length right coset representatives in $W\backslash W_p$. For $w\in W_p^+$, let $[w]$ be the right cell containing $w$, let $\mathcal{O}_{[w]}\subseteq\mathcal{N}$ be the nilpotent orbit corresponding to $[w]$ under the Lusztig bijection, and let $T(w\cdot 0)$ be the indecomposable tilting module of highest weight $w\cdot 0$. **Humphreys' conjecture.** If $p\geq h$, then for every $w\in W_p^+$,

$$
V_{G_1}(T(w\cdot 0))=\overline{\mathcal{O}_{[w]}}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the support varieties of indecomposable tilting modules realize the Lusztig bijection between right cells and nilpotent orbits. It is attributed to J.E. Humphreys and is presented here as a major problem motivating the computation of these support varieties.
record.source_name: William D. Hardesty, “On support varieties and the Humphreys conjecture in type A”, arXiv:1507.00970 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.00970

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2015). “However, Conjecture still remains open for all types, and still makes sense when $p < h$.”

record.title: The counting conjecture for $S_n$-fields with local conditions
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an $S_n$-field for $n\geq 3$ and signature $(r_1,r_2)$. Let $\mathcal S$ be a finite set of local conditions, and let $|\mathcal S|$ denote the product of their local densities. Write $L_n^{(r_2)}(X;\mathcal S)$ for the set of such fields with $|d_K|<X$ satisfying $\mathcal S$. **Counting conjecture.** There are positive constants $\delta<1$ and $\gamma$ such that

$$
|L_n^{(r_2)}(X)|=A(r_2)X+O(X^\delta),
$$

and

$$
|L_n^{(r_2)}(X;\mathcal S)|=|\mathcal S|A(r_2)X+O\left(\left(\prod_{p\in S}p\right)^\gamma X^\delta\right),
$$

with the implied constant uniformly bounded over the primes $p$ and the local conditions at $p$. This conjectural uniform counting estimate is used to obtain average results for Frobenius statistics and the smallest prime in a conjugacy class; the source does not provide evidence here that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Peter J. Cho and Henry H. Kim, “The average of the smallest prime in a conjugacy class”, arXiv:1601.03012 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03012

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2016).

record.title: The quasi-polynomiality conjecture for vanishing probabilities of Schur functions
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition, and let $P(s_\lambda\mapsto0)$ denote the probability that the Schur function $s_\lambda$ evaluates to zero over the finite field under consideration. A function $g:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ is a **quasi-polynomial** if there exists an integer $N>0$ and polynomials $g_0,g_1,\ldots,g_{N-1}\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $g(n)=g_i(n)$ whenever $n\equiv i\pmod N$. **The quasi-polynomiality conjecture.** For every partition $\lambda$, there exist a positive integer $k$ and a quasi-polynomial $f(q)$, depending on the residue class of $q$ modulo some integer, such that

$$
P(s_\lambda\mapsto0)=\frac{f(q)}{q^k}.
$$

The claim predicts a uniform arithmetic form for these vanishing probabilities as the finite-field parameter $q$ varies; the examples preceding the statement exhibit such residue-class-dependent formulas, but no general proof is provided here.
record.source_name: Ben Anzis, Shuli Chen, Yibo Gao, Jesse Kim, Zhaoqi Li and Rebecca Patrias, “Jacobi-Trudi determinants over finite fields”, arXiv:1611.00216 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.00216

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2016).

record.title: Girã o–Lewis–Popielarz conjecture on rainbow saturation of complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_r$ be the complete graph on $r$ vertices, let $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{R}(K_r))$ denote the minimum number of edges in an $n$-vertex edge-colored graph containing no rainbow copy of $K_r$ such that adding any non-edge in any color creates a rainbow copy of $K_r$, and fix $r\geq 3$. **Girã o–Lewis–Popielarz conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_r$ depending only on $r$ such that, for every $n\geq 2(r-2)$,

$$
\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{R}(K_r))=2(r-2)n+C_r.
$$

The conjecture predicts an exact linear formula for rainbow saturation with infinitely many available colors. It is refuted: for every $r\geq 3$, the paper establishes constants $\alpha_r$ satisfying $r+\Omega(r^{1/3})\leq\alpha_r\leq r+r^{1/2}$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal{R}(K_r))=\alpha_r n+O(1)$, contradicting the proposed slope $2(r-2)$.
record.source_name: Debsoumya Chakraborti, Kevin Hendrey, Ben Lund and Casey Tompkins, “Rainbow saturation for complete graphs”, arXiv:2212.04640 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04640

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: The strengthened monotonicity conjecture for multiplicities in $W_{n,n+K}$
record.statement: Let $K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\lambda\vdash 4K$, and write $\lambda^{(n-3K)}$ for the partition obtained by adding a first row of length $n-3K$ to $\lambda$. Let $m_{n,n+K}^{\lambda^{(n-3K)}}$ denote the multiplicity of the irreducible representation $S^{\lambda^{(n-3K)}}$ in $W_{n,n+K}$. **Strengthened monotonicity conjecture.** In Theorem, one can take $N_K=1$ and any $n\geq 3K$; equivalently, for every $K\in\mathbb{N}$, every partition $\lambda\vdash 4K$, and every $n\geq 3K$, the multiplicities form the asserted generally increasing sequence from this bound. The conjecture strengthens the preceding theorem, which establishes eventual general increase but does not identify the universal starting point. Its resolution would give uniform monotonicity beginning at the smallest proposed value of $N_K$.
record.source_name: Alon Romano, “On the T-ideal generated by the identity f=x^n”, arXiv:2212.05994 (2022).

record.title: Yang–Revin–Vdovin conjecture on conjugates detecting the pi-radical
record.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a fixed subset of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of all primes with $\pi'=\mathbb{P}\setminus\pi\ne\varnothing$. A **$\pi$-group** is a finite group whose order has all prime divisors in $\pi$. Set

$$
r=r(\pi)=\min\pi'
$$

and

$$
m=m(\pi)=\begin{cases}r,&r\in\{2,3\},\\r-1,&r\geqslant 5.\end{cases}
$$

For a finite group $G$, let $\operatorname{O}_\pi(G)$ denote its $\pi$-radical, the largest normal $\pi$-subgroup of $G$. **Yang–Revin–Vdovin conjecture.** In every finite group $G$, the $\pi$-radical $\operatorname{O}_\pi(G)$ coincides with the set

$$
\{x\in G\mid \langle x^{g_1},\dots,x^{g_m}\rangle\text{ is a }\pi\text{-group for all }g_1,\dots,g_m\in G\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a sharp Baer–Suzuki-type characterization of the $\pi$-radical using finitely many conjugates of an element. The paper invokes it while studying the case of almost simple groups with socle $\,{}^2F_4(q^2)'$, but does not establish the conjecture in full generality.
record.source_name: Danila O. Revin and Andrei V. Zavarnitsine, “On generations by conjugate elements in almost simple groups with socle ^2F_4(q^2)'”, arXiv:2212.13785 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.13785

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).

record.title: Bipartition-respecting packing coloring conjecture for hypercubes
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional hypercube. A packing coloring **respects bipartition** if all vertices assigned color $1$ lie in one part of the bipartition. Let $chi_\rho(Q_n)$ denote the packing chromatic number of $Q_n$, and let $chi_\rho^B(Q_n)$ denote the minimum number of colors in a packing coloring of $Q_n$ that respects its bipartition.

**Bipartition-respecting packing coloring conjecture.** For every $n\geq 0$,

$$
\chi_\rho(Q_n)=\chi_\rho^B(Q_n).
$$

The invariant $\chi_\rho^B(Q_n)$ is an upper bound for the packing chromatic number, and the conjecture asserts that requiring color $1$ to be contained in one bipartition class does not increase the minimum number of colors. The exact value of $\chi_\rho(Q_9)$ is still undetermined, so the conjecture concerns the relationship between these two parameters rather than a currently known exact value.
record.source_name: Petr Gregor, Jaka Kranjc, Borut Lužar and Kenny Štorgel, “Packing coloring of hypercubes with extended Hamming codes”, arXiv:2312.14576 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14576

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2023).

record.title: Char $p$ Mumford–Tate conjecture for ordinary abelian schemes
record.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a geometric connected smooth variety over $\mathbb{F}_q$, let $f_0:X_0\rightarrow \mathscr{A}_{g,\mathbb{F}_q}^{{\mathrm{ord}}}$ be a morphism as above, and let $A$ be the pullback abelian scheme over $X_0$. Denote by $G_{\mathrm{B}}(A)$ the generic Mumford–Tate group of the smallest Shimura subvariety whose Zariski closure contains the image of $f_0$. For $l\neq p$, let $G_l(A)$ be the $l$-adic étale monodromy group, and let $G_p(A)$ be the $p$-adic overconvergent crystalline monodromy group. **Char $p$ Mumford–Tate conjecture.** One has

$$
G_l(A)^\circ=G_{\mathrm{B}}(A)_{\mathbb{Q}_l}
$$

for every $l\neq p$, and

$$
G_p(A)^\circ=G_{\mathrm{B}}(A)_{\mathbb{Q}_p}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the connected $l$-adic and $p$-adic monodromy groups of an ordinary abelian scheme in characteristic $p$ coincide with the corresponding realizations of its generic Mumford–Tate group. It is presented as a monodromy conjecture in the paper; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ruofan Jiang, “p-adic monodromy and mod p unlikely intersections, II”, arXiv:2512.00687 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00687

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

record.title: Donald's uniqueness and variational conjecture for the homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère equation
record.statement:
Let $V$ be the compact complex manifold underlying the forms in the statement, let $R$ be a compact Riemann surface with boundary, and let $\rho:V\times\partial R\to\mathbf{R}$ satisfy that $\omega_0-\sqrt{-1}\,\overline{\partial}\partial\rho$ is a strictly positive $(1,1)$-form on each slice $V\times\{z\}$ for every $z\in\partial R$. Let $\mathcal{S}_\rho$ be the set of functions $\Phi$ on $V\times R$ equal to $\rho$ on the boundary and such that $\omega_0-\sqrt{-1}\,\overline{\partial}\partial\Phi$ is strictly positive on every slice $V\times\{w\}$, $w\in R$. **Donald's conjecture.** There is a unique solution $\Phi\in\mathcal{S}_\rho$ of the homogeneous complex Monge–Ampère equation

$$
(\Omega_0-\sqrt{-1}\,\overline{\partial}\partial\Phi)^{n+1}=0,
$$

and this solution realizes the absolute minimum of the functional $I_\rho$. This conjecture concerns the Dirichlet problem governing geodesics in the space of Kähler metrics; the supplied text gives no evidence that the asserted existence, uniqueness, or minimizing property has been resolved.
record.source_name: Xiuxiong Chen, “The Space of Kaehler metrics”, arXiv:math/0007057 (2000).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0007057

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2000).
